q: Which agile method is best known for technical practices such as pair programming, test-first programming and refactoring?
explanation: XP is most known for popularizing a holistic set of practices intended to improve the results of software projects, including pair programming, test-first programming and refactoring.

q: What are the five core values of XP?
options: Transparency, inspection, adaptation, trust, sustainable speed
explanation: XP's core values are communication, simplicity, feedback, courage and respect. The first option lists the Scrum values.

q: Two developers work together at one computer: one writes the code while the other reviews it, and they swap regularly. What is this practice?
options: Continuous integration of each day's work
explanation: Pair programming is a primary XP technical practice in which two people develop the same piece of work together.

q: A developer says she will spend the afternoon refactoring the billing module. What will she be doing?
options: Adding new features to the code
Improving the internal structure of the code without changing what it does
explanation: Refactoring improves the design of existing code while keeping its behavior the same, which keeps the code easy to change.

q: A team practises test-first programming. A developer is about to write a function that calculates tax. When does she write its test?
options: Only when a defect is found
Before the code it will test
explanation: In test-first programming, also called test-driven development, the test is written before the code, and just enough code is then written to pass it.

q: What is the main aim of lean management?
options: To complete as many projects as possible
To maximize customer value while minimizing waste
To write complete documentation before development starts
To fix the scope at the start
explanation: Lean management is a philosophy aimed at maximizing customer value while minimizing waste across all operations.

q: A startup is unsure whether anyone wants its idea. It builds the smallest version it can test and shows it to ten customers. In Lean Startup, what is this minimum viable product (MVP)?
options: The smallest testable version of an idea, used to collect real customer data
The final product with all features
The cheapest product on the market
explanation: Teams create the smallest testable version of the idea and cycle through a build–measure–learn loop to collect real customer data.

q: Testing an MVP shows that customers do not want the product as designed. The team changes direction before investing more. What is this called?
explanation: In Lean Startup, the results either confirm the team's assumptions or reveal the need to pivot: change direction before investing further time and money.

q: What does the word "kanban" mean?
explanation: The word kanban is literally translated as visual sign or card. Kanban boards with cards make the flow of work visible to everyone.

q: A team puts its work on a board with columns and agrees that no more than three items may be in testing at once. Which core property of the Kanban Method is this?
options: A product owner and scrum master
A sprint review every two weeks
explanation: The core properties are: visualize the workflow, limit WIP, manage flow, make process policies explicit, implement feedback loops and improve collaboratively.

q: How does the Kanban Method differ from most other agile approaches?
options: It does not prescribe timeboxed iterations
It forbids delivering to the customer
It requires a detailed plan to be approved up front
explanation: Unlike most agile approaches, the Kanban Method does not prescribe timeboxed iterations. Items are pulled through the process continuously.

q: On a kanban board, the "Test" column has a WIP limit of 3 and already holds 3 items. A developer finishes coding another item. What should happen?
options: Put the item in Test anyway
The team helps finish the items in Test before pulling more work in
explanation: In the Kanban Method it is more important to complete work than to start new work. The team works together to respect WIP limits and get each item to done.

q: A tester has just finished her item and is free. A manager wants to push three new items into testing at once. In a pull system, when does a new item enter a stage of work?
options: At the start of each month
When the customer demands that it be started at once
When the team has finished an item and has capacity
explanation: The Kanban Method uses a pull system: when the team completes an item, it can pull a new item into that spot.

q: A support team receives requests at unpredictable times and cannot commit to a fixed two-week plan. Which approach fits best?
explanation: The Kanban Method is useful when work arrives unpredictably and teams cannot make predictable commitments, even for short periods.

q: Which method is a family of methodologies whose rigor is chosen by the number of people on the project and its criticality, identified by colors?
explanation: Crystal is a family of methodologies designed to scale by project size and criticality. Different colors (Clear, Yellow, Orange, Red) mark the weight of the methodology.

q: Which framework is best known for fixing time, cost and quality at the outset and prioritizing scope to fit those constraints?
explanation: DSDM is best known for constraint-driven delivery: cost, quality and time are set at the outset and scope is formally prioritized to meet them.

q: In feature-driven development, what is a "feature"?
options: A large phase of the project
A defect found by the customer in testing
A small capability with business value
explanation: In FDD, feature refers to a small, business-value capability. The project is organized around building a features list and then planning, designing and building by feature.

q: Four Scrum teams work on the same product. A representative from each meets two or three times a week to coordinate work and remove impediments between teams. What is this?
explanation: Scrum of Scrums is used when two or more Scrum teams need to coordinate. A representative from each team reports completed work, next work and impediments.

q: Which statement describes Large Scale Scrum (LeSS)?
options: Several teams share one product backlog, one product owner, one definition of done and one sprint
Each team has its own product owner and backlog
It is a family of methods identified by colors
explanation: LeSS keeps as much of single-team Scrum as possible: one product backlog, one definition of done, one shippable increment, one product owner and one sprint for all teams.

q: How are Scrum and XP best described in relation to each other?
options: They are two names for the same method
Scrum focuses on managing the work; XP focuses on engineering practices, and the two are often combined
XP is for hardware and Scrum is for software
explanation: Scrum provides roles, events and artifacts. XP provides technical practices. Many teams use Scrum as the framework and XP practices inside it.
ref: Agile Practice Guide, 3.11; Agile Practice Guide, A3.3

q: A lean coach reviews a team's work and finds half-built features waiting unfinished, and two features that no customer requested. Which of the following is waste in the lean sense?
options: A feature that the customer uses every working day
Partially done work and features nobody asked for
explanation: Waste is anything that does not add value for the customer, such as partially done work, extra features, waiting, handoffs and defects.
ref: Effective Project Management, Chapter 11, What Is Lean Agile Project Management?; Agile Practice Guide, 2.3

links.label: Effective Project Management, Chapter 11, What Is Lean Agile Project Management?

q: Why is the Kanban Method called the "start where you are" method?
options: It requires new roles before starting
It begins with the current process, roles and titles and improves step by step
It can only be used at the start of a project
It starts with a full reorganization of teams, roles and reporting lines up front
explanation: Its defining principles are to start with the current state, pursue incremental change and respect current processes, roles and titles, so it is less disruptive to adopt.

q: A team works in short sprints, shows its stories on a kanban board with WIP limits, and has no named roles. It holds a planning session whenever the number of cards in progress falls below five. Which approach is this, and what is that rule called?
options: Scrumban, and the rule is a planning trigger
Scrum, and the rule is the sprint goal
Crystal Clear, and the rule is osmotic planning
DSDM, and the rule is a timebox
explanation: Scrumban uses Scrum as the framework and Kanban for process improvement. A planning trigger tells the team when to plan next, typically when work in progress falls below a set level. There are no predefined roles.
ref: Agile Practice Guide, First Edition, A3.6

links.label: Agile Practice Guide, First Edition, A3.6

q: Before building a feature, the developers, the tester and the product owner sit down together and agree its acceptance criteria. They then create the tests, and only afterwards build just enough to pass them. Which practice is this?
explanation: In acceptance test-driven development (ATDD) the entire team discusses the acceptance criteria for a work product, then creates the tests, which lets the team write just enough to meet the criteria.

q: A large software project names a chief architect, a chief programmer, several class owners and a domain expert, and plans, designs and builds one small capability at a time. Which approach is it using?
explanation: Feature-driven development has six primary roles: project manager, chief architect, development manager, chief programmer, class owner and domain expert. Its five processes include plan by feature, design by feature and build by feature.
ref: Agile Practice Guide, First Edition, A3.7

links.label: Agile Practice Guide, First Edition, A3.7

q: A company wants something between Scrum, which it finds too narrow, and a heavier process it finds too prescriptive. It picks a process decision framework whose principles include people-first, goal-driven and enterprise awareness. Which is it?
explanation: The 2017 guide describes Disciplined Agile as a process decision framework that blends agile practices, balanced between methods that are too narrow (Scrum) and too prescriptive (AgileUP). Its principles are people-first, learning-oriented, full delivery life cycle, goal-driven, enterprise awareness and scalable.
ref: Agile Practice Guide, First Edition, A3.14

links.label: Agile Practice Guide, First Edition, A3.14

q: Three Scrum teams send one member each to a coordination meeting twice a week. Besides completed work, next work and current impediments, what else does each representative report?
options: Each developer's hours for the week
The velocity of the other teams
Upcoming impediments that might block the other teams
The budget that remains for the release and for each of the teams
explanation: In a Scrum of Scrums each representative reports completed work, the next set of work, current impediments, and potential upcoming impediments that might block the other teams.
ref: Agile Practice Guide, First Edition, A3.10.1

links.label: Agile Practice Guide, First Edition, A3.10.1

q: A department head fears that adopting the Kanban Method will abolish job titles and reorganize his teams. Which of the method's defining principles, as the 2017 Agile Practice Guide lists them, answers this fear?
options: Make every process policy explicit and visible to the whole of the organization
Respect the current process, roles, responsibilities and titles
explanation: The Kanban Method's defining principles are: start with the current state; agree to pursue incremental, evolutionary change; respect the current process, roles, responsibilities and titles; and encourage acts of leadership at all levels. The others listed are core properties.
ref: Agile Practice Guide, First Edition, A3.4
